A satellite or launcher has to work for its whole design life on the reliability it was built with, so the analysis has to be right before it flies — and the standards say as much: ECSS-Q-ST-30-11C for derating, NASA EEE-INST-002 for part selection, with radiation, vacuum and thermal cycling on top of the usual stresses. That makes the shift-left case sharper here than anywhere else: component derating and stress analysis at the schematic stage, failure modes and their effects traced from part to mission function, and redundancy modelled rather than assumed, because a redundant string that shares a failure mode is one string. Long programmes bring their own problem — parts go out of production between design and launch — so traceable analyses that can be re-run against a replacement part are worth more than a one-off report. jobs.description: Loading… WHAT YOU WILL DO Run reliability analyses on customer hardware: MTBF prediction, electrical stress and de-rating, FMECA, RBD and schematic review. Review schematics and BOMs for design weaknesses that a standard DRC does not catch, and write up what you found so a customer's engineers can act on it. Turn what you learn on real boards into rules and component data inside fiXtress®, CircuitHawk® and the Synthelyzer™ ECAD plugin, so the next analysis finds it automatically. Work alongside our AI: help build and grade the prompts, datasets and checks that let a model read a schematic, a datasheet or a BOM — and be the engineer who says whether its answer is right. Replace your own manual steps. An analysis that takes a week by hand is the raw material for the next feature; you are expected to automate yourself out of the repetitive parts and say what should be automated next. Work directly with customers' engineering teams during a project, and with our software engineers on what the tools should do next. WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR B.Sc. in Electrical or Electronic Engineering. Several years of hands-on engineering behind you. Hands-on electronic circuit design or design verification — you can read a schematic and say what will fail first. Comfortable with component datasheets, stress ratings and de-rating standards. Demonstrated process improvement: something you made faster, more repeatable or less error-prone, and what it looked like before and after. Practical use of AI in your own engineering work — what you use it for, where you do not trust it, and how you check it. Scripting in Python, MATLAB or similar is a strong plus. An interest in reliability engineering: MIL-HDBK-217, IEC 61508, DO-254 and their relatives. Experience with them is welcome, and willingness to learn them counts. English good enough to write a report a customer will read. jobs.description: Loading… WHAT YOU WILL DO Design and ship across the stack: the Windows desktop applications engineers run every day, the calculation engines behind them, and the web tools and services that put a piece of it in a browser. Build AI into the product — turning engineering artefacts (schematics, netlists, BOMs, CAD exports, reliability standards) into analysis a customer can trust and act on. Build AI into how we work: agent-assisted code review, automated regression and UI validation, ticket triage, documentation, customer-data extraction. You set the standard for using it in a way that is safe and verifiable. Find the recurring friction — manual releases, flaky validation, hand-built installers, copy-paste support workflows — and replace it with something automated and boring. Work on calculation code where the answer has to be right: results feed certification evidence, so correctness is a requirement rather than a goal. Raise the bar on CI/CD, test coverage, telemetry and release quality across products, and mentor the engineers around you without needing authority to do it. WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR B.Sc. in Computer Science or Software Engineering, or the equivalent in what you have shipped, plus several years of production experience. Solid programming in one or more of C++, C#, Python or TypeScript/JavaScript, and comfort moving between them. Demonstrated process improvement. Expect to be asked for two or three specific things you changed — a pipeline, a test strategy, a release process — and what they looked like before and after. Proven hands-on use of AI in real work, not "I have tried an autocomplete plugin": agent-driven workflows you built, what they automated, how you constrained them, and how you verified the output when it mattered. Comfortable with data structures, algorithms and numerical code — much of what we ship is graph and probability work with a UI on top. Able to own a feature end to end, from what it should do to it being in a release, and to write a design note or a release summary another engineer will actually read. Knowledge of electronics — circuits, components, PCB and CAD data, BOMs, EDA tooling — is a real advantage, as is exposure to reliability or safety standards such as MIL-HDBK-217, IEC 61508, ISO 26262 and DO-254. About BQR Where we started We began in 1989 as a consultancy, on the Lavi aircraft programme, and grew into a software company. The job has not really changed since: help engineers build systems that fail less, and that are cheaper to keep running when they do. What shift-left means Schematic verification, stress and derating analysis, RAMS modelling and maintenance planning, in one toolchain. Fewer respins, shorter release cycles, and a product your field team can actually support. Built on patents The simulation and analysis algorithms behind the products are covered by several patents. They have been through more than 4,500 projects. Our Methodology: Shift-Left Reliability 1 Design-phase checks Catch preventable schematic issues before PCB layout and first-article build. 2 Quantified stress and derating Check that every component stays inside its margins across the whole mission profile. 3 RAMS digital twin Model functions, failure modes and maintenance to forecast availability and risk. 4 Maintenance optimization Plan the spares and the tasks that keep downtime and lifecycle cost down. 5 End-to-end traceability From the ECAD check through to RAMS results and field maintenance KPIs.
